blocks.text: Adhérences et signes indélébiles is an exploration of the body as an emotional archive, and of the possibility of transforming a wound into a new visual language. The project began after a series of surgeries — including one for a malignant tumor — that left deep marks on my body, both visible and invisible. I felt the need to create a self portrait that was not a document of pain, but an evocative gesture: a way to give meaning back to what had shaped my story. This process resonates with the philosophy of Kintsugi. Healing is slow; it reveals fragility, but also the strength to endure. An object does not return “as new”: it returns truer, carrying the story of its fracture and its rebirth. With this same gaze, I began working on my own scars — not to hide them, but to transform them, allowing softness and light to enter where there had been pain and suffering. Over time, the project — born from my body — opened itself to other people and their wounds. Before each photograph, there is a moment of listening: a quiet space in which the element that accompanies their story can emerge. The images take shape from the fusion of two photographs: the scar, and an element chosen for its ability to evoke inner calm. Sometimes it is a landscape; other times, a place or an object that belongs to the person’s history, something that holds an intimate resonance. “Adhérences et signes indélébiles” grows from this: from the marks that remain beneath the skin, from the traces you cannot ignore, from everything the body preserves even when the mind would rather forget. It is a title that speaks of wounds, but also of transformation — of the way pain becomes image, and the image becomes a way to restore meaning to what has been inscribed.

Since its inception, Adhérences et Signes Indélébiles has been presented in several artistic and photographic contexts, notably in Arles as part of the Off programme of the Rencontres de la Photographie, in Rome through exhibitions organised by the Tevere Art Gallery, at Paratissima in Turin and, in 2025, in a solo exhibition accompanied by a creative workshop at the Magma Museum in Civitanova Marche. The project has also been the focus of several public talks and discussions, notably during Rome Future Week and at Paratissima. The series has received several international recognitions, including a Bronze Medal at the Fotoslovo Awards. It was notably awarded the Commended Prize in the Series Category at the 2022 Creative Photo Awards, a distinction recognising the strength and coherence of the series.
